core.title: Player transport controls
core.guidance: Play/pause, seek slider with time readout and keyboard/remote stepping, skip ±10 s, next/previous where relevant, captions and audio track selectors, quality only if user-facing, live indicator and go-to-live for live streams, volume on web/desktop only (TV uses the remote), controls overlay auto-hides except while focused/hovered; every control labelled; captions styling respects system preferences.
core.avoid_when: Never custom-build when the platform control set already meets the need and the brand allows it.

implementation.compose-tv: Media3 with a Compose overlay; KEYCODE handling for media keys; focusRequester on play/pause.

core.title: Broadcast guide (TV)
core.guidance: Top tabs (Live, Guide, Catch-up, Search), a fast EPG grid with a now-line and channel logos, landscape channel cards with live badges, condensed titles with tabular times, flat tonal surfaces so text stays legible over 200 channels, focus border + scale (no glow needed), mini-player while browsing. Identity via the guide's colour coding of genres and the channel-card treatment.
core.use_when: Live-TV-first products: many channels, EPG, catch-up, sports; users switch fast and read schedules.
core.avoid_when: On-demand-first catalogues with rich art (use 'Cinematic media').

core.title: EPG / programme guide
core.guidance: See the EPG grid pattern for structure; component specifics: cell shows title + time with ellipsis, minimum cell width so 5-minute programmes stay focusable (with a time label on focus), current programme highlighted and the 'now' line updates every minute, channel column sticky with logo + number, day picker above the grid, focus moves by programme not by pixel, long press or a key opens programme detail with record/remind actions, jump-to-now shortcut, mini preview of the focused channel optional.
core.avoid_when: On-demand only catalogues; phones in portrait (use a per-channel list).

implementation.compose-tv: Custom LazyLayout or LazyRow-of-LazyColumn sharing horizontal scroll; measure cells from time deltas; use Modifier.focusProperties to override up/down to the same time slot.

guardrails.title: Only the happy state was designed
guardrails.guidance: Enumerate states per screen and per interactive component before implementation and verify each visually; test with long strings, zero items, 10k items, and slow networks.
guardrails.use_when: Screens with no empty, loading, error, offline, partial, or long-text states; buttons with no pressed/disabled/loading states; TV cards with no focused state.
guardrails.selected_for: required concern states: every screen ships empty/loading/error states

guardrails.title: TV: exactly one visible focus at all times
guardrails.guidance: Set initial focus deterministically (first actionable content or Play on detail), restore focus to the previously focused item when returning, keep focus on screen (scroll into view), move focus to a sensible neighbour when the focused item is removed, and never rely on colour tint alone for the focused state.
guardrails.use_when: Every TV screen, after every navigation, after data loads, after dialogs close, after list updates.
guardrails.avoid_when: Never leave focus on a hidden or off-screen element; never let focus disappear after a list refresh.
guardrails.selected_for: required concern accessibility: platform accessibility baseline

guardrails.title: TV: focus response and list performance
guardrails.guidance: Focus moves must render within one frame (≤16 ms at 60 Hz) even while images load; key events are never dropped or coalesced into jumps; images sized to card, cached, and loaded with placeholders; rows virtualised vertically and horizontally; heavy backdrops debounced; test on the cheapest target device (e.g. 1–2 GB RAM set-top boxes), not the emulator.
guardrails.use_when: Rails, grids, EPG, any list on TV; especially with images.
guardrails.avoid_when: Never decode full-size artwork for thumbnails; never render all rails at once.
guardrails.selected_for: required concern performance: focus latency and catalog virtualization on TV

guardrails.title: TV: 10-foot typography
guardrails.guidance: Body ≥24 sp (Android) / ≥29 pt (tvOS) at 1080p design scale, captions ≥20 sp, titles 32–48, display 57–72; sans with large x-height and open counters; short strings (titles ≤2 lines, synopsis ≤3 lines with expansion); avoid thin weights (<400) and light text on busy imagery; line height ≥1.3.
guardrails.avoid_when: Never scale a desktop type ramp up by a factor; rebuild the scale for distance and for reduced text volume.

guardrails.title: TV: overscan-safe margins
guardrails.guidance: Keep interactive and text content ≥5% from edges: at the 960×540 dp design frame that is 48 dp horizontal and 27 dp vertical (Android guidance: up to 58/28 dp for maximum safety; tvOS: 60 pt sides, 60 pt top/bottom on the 1920×1080 frame). Let rails scroll under the margin so partial cards hint at more content.
guardrails.use_when: All persistent UI (nav, titles, buttons, subtitles); backgrounds and artwork may bleed.
guardrails.avoid_when: Do not inset full-bleed imagery; do not rely on the panel reporting overscan.
